To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N-linked glycans of JUNV glycoproteins play an important role in the trafficking and surface expression of the glycoprotein and are important for the attenuation of the live vaccine.

the live-attenuation of the Argentine hemorrhagic fever vaccine, Candid #1 ( Can ) strain, is due to the presence of an amino acid substitution in the glycoprotein gene that results in its improper processing and trafficking to the cell surface.

the N-linked glycans of the Junin virus glycoprotein are important for its trafficking and surface expression, and the absence of this motif results in its improper processing and reduced surface expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanisms of attenuation and immunogenicities of live-attenuation JUNV vaccines and the identification of the molecular determinants of the Can GPC responsible for its altered protein processing, which may be useful for the rational design and development of novel live-attenuative JUNV vaccine candidates.
the mechanisms of attenuation of the Can vaccine strain, which is the first attenuated vaccine for AHF.
the identification of the mechanisms underlying attenuation of the Can vaccine, which will facilitate the development of novel live-attenuating JUNV strains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N-linked glycans at amino acid positions T168 in JUNV G1 and N169 in G2 are important for the proper processing and trafficking of JUNVs GPC to the surface of infected cells.
the N-linked motif at amino acid position 166–168 in JUNV G1 is important for GPC trafficking to the cell surface and the proper release of GPC from the ER.
the absence of the N-linked glycan motif at amino acid 168 of the JUNV G1 domain is a key molecular determinant of Can GPC attenuation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Can GPC gene contains a single point mutation (T168A) that results in a change of an N-linked glycoylation motif, and this single point mutation is responsible for the attenuation of the virus in guinea pigs.
the N-linked glycans in G1 and G2 are critical for the trafficking of GPC to the plasma membrane.
the N-linked glycans in JUNV G1 are not essential for virus replication, but rather they may play important roles in GPC processing, ER retention and cell surface expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GPC of the Can strain is not processed properly and this contributes to its attenuated phenotype in the guinea pig model.
the N-linked glycans in the GPC are important for the processing and trafficking of JUNVs GPC.

the GPC of the Can vaccine strain is differentially processed, which results in reduced surface expression of GPC, a finding that may be important for the attenuation and immunological properties of the live-attenuate vaccine strain.
